Keystone 5221 (+) / 5222 (−), "battery contacts for MOLDED CASES" — the family designed for exactly this: a plate screwed, staked or riveted to a plastic wall.

stop it rotating and spread the contact load into plastic. 0.2/side round the plate: the caps print OUTBOARD FACE DOWN, so the pocket floor is a clean TOP surface (no bridge).

2 EAR SLOTS — widen the pocket 1.2 mm further left and right at mid-height. That is where Keystone's two struck-out side ears sit. In an injection-moulded case they bite; in printed PETG just let them locate.

A cylindrical-cell contact is sized to the cell's END FACE, not its diameter: the 10.8 × 12.7 plate touches the middle of a Ø26 flat top exactly as it touches a Ø18 one. What changes with cell size in Keystone's

catalogue is the compartment length "L", and that is our printed part. Buy the real 5221/5222 from DigiKey/Mouser rather than an Amazon assortment though — 8 contacts is a ~$5 line item and it guarantees the

⚠ The real cost of springs: resistance, not length
⚠ The real cost of springs: resistance, not length

Published measurements of 18650-holder spring contacts run 30-100 mΩ each. Four in series at our 2.6 A pack current is 0.3-1.0 V and 0.8-2.7 W — up to 8 % of a 12.8 V pack, as heat, inside the tube. A soldered

Published measurements of 18650-holder spring contacts run 30-100 mΩ each. Four in series at our 2.6 A pack current is 0.3-1.0 V and 0.8-2.7 W — up to 8 % of a 12.8 V pack, as heat, inside the tube. A soldered

nickel-strip pack has none of this; it is the actual price of user-replaceable cells. The standard fix is a SPRING BYPASS: a loose strand of fine tinned copper soldered from the spring's base coil to its tip coil,

nickel-strip pack has none of this; it is the actual price of user-replaceable cells. The standard fix is a SPRING BYPASS: a loose strand of fine tinned copper soldered from the spring's base coil to its tip coil,

longer than the spring so it never fights the travel. It solders because the spring is nickel PLATED — the same reason nickel strip wets in a second on this bench while the cell caps refused to wet at all.

longer than the spring so it never fights the travel. It solders because the spring is nickel PLATED — the same reason nickel strip wets in a second on this bench while the cell caps refused to wet at all.
TO DO — MEASURE a real 5222 four-wire at 2.6 A before committing. It is one number and it decides whether the bypass is optional or mandatory.
